title: "Classwork_strings"
format: html

```{r}
library(here)
library(tidyverse)
library(tidytext)
library(wordcloud)
library(janeaustenr)
```

```{r}
seq_data <- c("ATCCCGTC")
str_sub(seq_data, start = 3, end = 5) <- "A" # add an A in the 3rd position
seq_data
```
```{r}
str_dup(seq_data, times = c(4, 4)) # times is the number of times to duplicate each string
```
```{r}
badtreatments <- c("High", " High", "High ", "Low", "Low")
badtreatments

str_trim(badtreatments) # this removes both

```
```{r}
x <- "oh boy r is so cool"

str_to_title(x)
```

```{r}
data <- c("AAA", "TATA", "CTAG", "GCTT")

# find all the strings with an A
str_view(data, pattern = "A", use_escapes = FALSE)
str_detect(data, pattern = "AT")
str_locate(data, pattern = "AT")


```

```{r}
#Meta Characters

vals <- c("a.b", "b.c", "c.d")

# string, pattern, replace
str_replace(vals, "\\.", " ")

#the backslash means ESCAPE so you can use a metacharacter
```
```{r}
vals <- c("a.b.c", "b.c.d", "c.d.e")
# string, pattern, replace
str_replace_all(vals, "\\.", " ")

#use _all for any str functions in order to apply it to more than the first

```
```{r}
val2 <- c("test 123", "test 456", "test")

str_subset(val2, "\\d")

#\\d subsets the data to those that have digits
```
```{r}
str_count(val2, "[aeiou]")

# count any digit
str_count(val2, "[0-9]")
```
```{r}
strings <- c("550-153-7578",
             "banana",
             "435.114.7586",
             "home: 672-442-6739")

phone <- "([2-9][0-9]{2})[- .]([0-9]{3})[- .]([0-9]{4})"

# Which strings contain phone numbers?
str_detect(strings, phone)

```

```{r}
# subset only the strings with phone numbers
test <- str_subset(strings, phone)
test
```

```{r}
clean_phone <- test |>
  str_remove_all(("\\:")) |>
  str_remove_all("[[:alpha:]]") |>
    str_trim() |>
  str_replace_all("\\D", "-") 


clean_phone
  
  
  
```
```{r}
# explore it
head(austen_books())
```

```{r}
original_books <- austen_books() |>
  group_by(book) |>
  mutate(line = row_number(),
         chapter = cumsum(str_detect(text, regex("^chapter [\\divxlc]", #Things that start with the word Chapter, and have a number (or roman numeral) after it
                                                 ignore_case = TRUE)))) |>
  ungroup()




```
```{r}
tidy_books <- original_books |>
  unnest_tokens(output = word, input = text)

head(tidy_books)
```

```{r}
head(get_stopwords())
```
```{r}
cleaned_books <- tidy_books |>
  anti_join(get_stopwords()) # dataframe without the stopwords

head(cleaned_books)
```
```{r}
#couting the most common words

cleaned_books |>
  count(word, sort = TRUE)
```

```{r}
sent_word_counts <- tidy_books |>
  inner_join(get_sentiments()) |> # only keep pos or negative words
  count(word, sentiment, sort = TRUE) # count them

head(sent_word_counts)[1:3, ]
```

```{r}
sent_word_counts |>
  filter(n > 150) |> # take only if there are over 150 instances of it
  mutate(n = ifelse(sentiment == "negative", -n, n)) |> # add a column where if the word is negative make the count negative
  mutate(word = reorder(word, n)) |> # sort it so it goes from largest to smallest
  ggplot(aes(x = n, y = word, fill = sentiment)) +
  geom_col() +
  labs(y = "Contribution to sentiment")

```

```{r}
words <- cleaned_books |>
  count(word) |> # count all the words
  arrange(desc(n)) |> # sort the words
  slice(1:100) # take the top 100

wordcloud(words = words$word, freq = words$n, colors = brewer.pal(8, "Dark2"))


#wordcloud 2 makes an HTML widget.
```
